title: Middle East (UAE, Saudi Arabia) AI-chip imports and fab ambitions: US licensing conditions, sovereign AI data-centre deals and local industrial policy
why_it_matters: From 2025 the Gulf became a major destination for US AI accelerators under licence conditions (e.g. Commerce licences to G42 and Humain in Nov 2025), with state-backed buyers, security safeguards and investment pledges tied to chip access. This is a new demand centre, a test case for US AI-chip export policy and a potential future fab/OSAT location; no existing unit covers it beyond one line in RU-0245.
questions: What US export licences, conditions and security safeguards govern AI-chip shipments to the UAE and Saudi Arabia (volumes, recipients such as G42 and Humain, reporting requirements), and how did they evolve after the AI Diffusion Rule rescission?
What government-to-government agreements and investment pledges (e.g. US-UAE AI partnership, Stargate UAE, Saudi Humain) are tied to chip access, and what do the official texts actually commit?
What local industrial policy exists for chip design, fabs or OSAT in the UAE and Saudi Arabia (sovereign funds such as MGX/PIF, announced projects, incentives), and what has actually been built?
How large is Gulf AI-accelerator demand relative to global supply (announced MW/GW and chip counts), with dates and sources?
What diversion or security concerns have regulators or legislators raised about Gulf deployments (China ties, re-export), and how are they monitored?
subquestions: Which UAE/Saudi agencies administer export control and data-centre security rules?
Which Gulf sovereign funds hold stakes in foundries or chip firms (e.g. GlobalFoundries ownership by Mubadala)?
primary_sources: commerce.gov and bis.gov press releases and Federal Register notices
White House fact sheets on US-UAE and US-Saudi agreements
UAE and Saudi government ministry releases
open_questions: Planner-flagged gap (plan1-A-9d62, plan1-D-8e05); confirmed by gap-plan-6a1d search that US Commerce licensed GB300-class exports to G42 and Humain in Nov 2025 (to verify against commerce.gov).
